63062-terror-out-of-space.title: Terror Out Of Space
63062-terror-out-of-space.creator: Unknown
63062-terror-out-of-space.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. it was very, very cold in spite of the sweltering heat in the cabin, and it had a nasty habit of yanking itself tight every few minutes, causing Lundy to jerk and sweat as though he'd been spiked.

73379-in-the-brush.title: In The Southwest.
73379-in-the-brush.creator: Unknown
73379-in-the-brush.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "And so you are a Western missionary. Well, do tell me if anything _strange_ or _funny_ ever _did_ happen to a missionary. Mother has taken the home-missionary papers ever since I was a child, and I always read them; and I often wonder if anything _strange_ or _funny_ did _ever_ happen to a Western missionary."

arxiv-2104-07237.title: Skilled and Mobile: Survey Evidence of AI Researchers’ Immigration Preferences
arxiv-2104-07237.creator: Remco Zwetsloot, Baobao Zhang, Noemi Dreksler, Lauren Kahn, Markus Anderljung, Allan Dafoe, Michael C. Horowitz
arxiv-2104-07237.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Remco Zwetsloot, Baobao Zhang, Noemi Dreksler, Lauren Kahn, Markus Anderljung, Allan Dafoe, Michael C. Horowitz. Countries, companies, and universities are increasingly competing over top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) researchers. Where are these researchers likely to immigrate and what affects their immigration decisions?

arxiv-2108-01532.title: Effective Model Integration Algorithm for Improving Link and Sign Prediction in Complex Networks
arxiv-2108-01532.creator: Chuang Liu, Shimin Yu, Ying Huang, Zi-Ke Zhang
arxiv-2108-01532.description: Abstract Link and sign prediction in complex networks bring great help to decision-making and recommender systems, such as in predicting potential relationships or relative status levels. Many previous studies focused on designing the special algorithms to perform either link prediction or sign prediction.

arxiv-2204-03432.title: Collective patterns and stable misunderstandings in networks striving for consensus without a common value system
arxiv-2204-03432.creator: Johannes Falk, Edwin Eichler, Katja Windt, Marc-Thorsten Hütt
arxiv-2204-03432.description: Abstract Collective phenomena in systems of interacting agents have helped us understand diverse social, ecological and biological observations. The corresponding explanations are challenged by incorrect information processing. In particular, the models typically assume a shared understanding of signals or a common truth or value system, i.e., an agreement of whether the measurement or perception of information is ‘right’ or ‘wrong’.

arxiv-2204-06718.title: Learning Convolutional Neural Networks in the Frequency Domain
arxiv-2204-06718.creator: Hengyue Pan, Yixin Chen, Xin Niu, Wenbo Zhou, Dongsheng Li
arxiv-2204-06718.description: Abstract Convolutional neural network (CNN) has achieved impressive success in computer vision during the past few decades. The image convolution operation helps CNNs to get good performance on image-related tasks. However, the image convolution has high computation complexity and hard to be implemented. This paper proposes the CEMNet, which can be trained in the frequency domain.

arxiv-2305-06219.title: Geometric characterization for cyclic heat engines far from equilibrium
arxiv-2305-06219.creator: Tan Van Vu, Keiji Saito
arxiv-2305-06219.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tan Van Vu, Keiji Saito. Considerable attention has been devoted to microscopic heat engines in both theoretical and experimental aspects. Notably, the fundamental limits pertaining to power and efficiency, as well as the tradeoff relations between these two quantities, have been intensively studied. This study aims to shed further light on the ultimate limits of heat engines by exploring the relationship between the geometric length along the path of cyclic heat engines operating at arbitrary speeds and their power and efficiency.

arxiv-2310-03548.title: A theoretical view of the T-web statistical description of the cosmic web
arxiv-2310-03548.creator: Emma Ayçoberry, Alexandre Barthelemy, Sandrine Codis
arxiv-2310-03548.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Emma Ayçoberry, Alexandre Barthelemy, Sandrine Codis. The objective classification of the cosmic web into different environments is an important aspect of large-scale structure studies, as it can be used as a tool to study the formation of structures (halos and galaxies) in mode detail, and it forms a link between their properties and the large-scale environment; these different environments also offer another class of objects whose statistics contain cosmological information.

arxiv-2405-00175.title: Towards a Search Engine for Machines: Unified Ranking for Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models Conference: Proceedings of the 47th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 14–18, 2024; Washington, DC, USA Proceedings of the 47th Inte
arxiv-2405-00175.creator: Alireza Salemi, Hamed Zamani
arxiv-2405-00175.description: Abstract . This paper introduces uRAG –a framework with a unified retrieval engine that serves multiple downstream retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. Each RAG system consumes the retrieval results for a unique purpose, such as open-domain question answering, fact verification, entity linking, and relation extraction.

arxiv-2406-13833.title: Cluster Quilting: Spectral Clustering for Patchwork Learning
arxiv-2406-13833.creator: Lili Zheng †, Andersen Chang †, Genevera I. Allen
arxiv-2406-13833.description: Abstract Patchwork learning arises as a new and challenging data collection paradigm where both samples and features are observed in fragmented subsets. Due to technological limits, measurement expense, or multimodal data integration, such patchwork data structures are frequently seen in neuroscience, healthcare, and genomics, among others.

arxiv-2505-13893.title: InfiGFusion: Graph-on-Logits Distillation via Efficient Gromov-Wasserstein for Model Fusion
arxiv-2505-13893.creator: Yuanyi Wang, Zhaoyi Yan, Yiming Zhang, Qi Zhou, Yanggan Gu, Fei Wu, Hongxia Yang
arxiv-2505-13893.description: Abstract Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have intensified efforts to fuse heterogeneous open-source models into a unified system that inherits their complementary strengths. Existing logit-based fusion methods maintain inference efficiency but treat vocabulary dimensions independently, overlooking semantic dependencies encoded by cross-dimension interactions.

arxiv-2506-17234.title: Graph Neural Networks in Multi-Omics Cancer Research: A Structured Survey
arxiv-2506-17234.creator: Payam Zohari, Mostafa Haghir Chehreghani
arxiv-2506-17234.description: Abstract The task of data integration for multi-omics data has emerged as a powerful strategy to unravel the complex biological underpinnings of cancer. Recent advancements in graph neural networks (GNNs) offer an effective framework to model heterogeneous and structured omics data, enabling precise representation of molecular interactions and regulatory networks.

arxiv-2511-10958.title: Text-guided Weakly Supervised Framework for Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition Journal: Pattern Recognition
arxiv-2511-10958.creator: Gunho Jung, Heejo Kong, Seong-Whan Lee
arxiv-2511-10958.description: Abstract Dynamic facial expression recognition (DFER) aims to identify emotional states by modeling the temporal changes in facial movements across video sequences. A key challenge in DFER is the many-to-one labeling problem, where a video composed of numerous frames is assigned a single emotion label.

arxiv-2511-15672.title: From Qubits to Couplings: A Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning Framework for LHC Physics
arxiv-2511-15672.creator: Marwan Ait Haddou, Mohamed Belfkir, Salah Eddine El Harrauss
arxiv-2511-15672.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning (HyQML) framework to improve the sensitivity of double Higgs boson searches in the H ​ H → b ​ b ¯ ​ γ ​ γ HH\to b\bar{b}\gamma\gamma final state at s = 13.6 ​ TeV \sqrt{s}=13.6~\text{TeV} .

arxiv-2602-05322.title: More on OTOCs and Chaos in Quantum Mechanics - Magnetic Fields
arxiv-2602-05322.creator: Cameron Beetar & Jeff Murugan
arxiv-2602-05322.description: Abstract We revisit thermal out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) in single-particle quantum systems, focusing on magnetic billiards. Using the stadium billiard as a testbed, we compute the thermal OTOC C T ​ ( t ) = − ⟨ [ x ⁡ ( t ) , p ] 2 ⟩ β C_{T}(t)=-\langle[x(t),p]^{2}\rangle_{\beta} and extract Lyapunov-like exponents λ L \lambda_{L} that quantify early-time growth.

britannica-1911-forkel-johann-nikolaus.title: Forkel, Johann Nikolaus (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-forkel-johann-nikolaus.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-forkel-johann-nikolaus.description: Article 'Forkel, Johann Nikolaus' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. musician, was born on the 22nd of February 1749 at Meeder in Coburg. He was the son of a cobbler, and as a practical musician, especially as a pianoforte player, achieved some eminence; but his claims to a more abiding name rest chiefly upon his literary skill and deep research as an historian of musical science and literature.

A 42-year-old premenopausal woman presented with a 10-year history of vertex pustules and crusts leading to scarring patches of alopecia. Nine years later, she presented pruritus in the frontal hairline.

pmc-10748269.title: Visual Features for Improving Endoscopic Bleeding Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
pmc-10748269.creator: Adam Brzeski, Tomasz Dziubich, Henryk Krawczyk
pmc-10748269.description: The presented paper investigates the problem of endoscopic bleeding detection in endoscopic videos in the form of a binary image classification task. A set of definitions of high-level visual features of endoscopic bleeding is introduced, which incorporates domain knowledge from the field.

pmc-11600869.title: Distribution of Candida species isolated from people living with human immunodeficiency virus with oropharyngeal and oral candidiasis in Africa in the era of universal test and treat policy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11600869.creator: Benson Musinguzi, Ekwaro A. Obuku, Alex Mwesigwa, Richard Migisha, Alison Annet Kinengyere, Regina Ndagire, Andrew Baguma, Erick Jacob Okek, Ronald Olum, Herbert Itabangi, Gerald Mboowa, Obondo James Sande, Beatrice Achan
pmc-11600869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe introduction of antiretroviral therapy (ART) and the implementation of the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) universal test and treat (UTT) policy have led to a decline in the incidence of opportunistic infections. However, oropharyngeal and oral candidiasis remain prevalent and continue to pose challenges among people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PLHIV) in Africa, indicating the need for a better understanding of the distribution of Candida species responsible for these infections.

pmc-12405856.title: Research trends in mobile payment adoption: Research trends and agenda
pmc-12405856.creator: Alejandro Valencia-Arias, Jesus Alberto Jimenez Garcia, Gustavo Moreno-López, Aaron José Alberto Oré León, Lucia Palacios-Moya, Jackeline Valencia, Martha Benjumea-Arias, Mohammad Rakibul Islam Bhuiyan, Lisa Mani, Ni Made Estiyanti, Wahyu Hidayat, JHOANY ALEJANDRO VALENCIA ARIAS, Ni Made Estiyanti,
pmc-12405856.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study explores the adoption of mobile payments as a research field to understand the technological, socioeconomic, and cultural factors that influence the understanding of the users’ experience and satisfaction and attract more users. It is vital to examine the research trends in the adoption of mobile payments from a systematic literature review using PRISMA 2020 to select 63 documents from Scopus and WOS. Among the results, the most used models for this analysis are extended TAM and extended UTAUT.

pmc-12644277.title: SLIT2 inhibits lung adenocarcinoma progression by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition
pmc-12644277.creator: Zhimeng Chen, Hu Chen, Yuan Cui, Jun Chen, Weibiao Zeng, Jian Yang, Yu Li, Xiaobei Peng, Xin Tong, Jun Zhao
pmc-12644277.description: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the most common subtype of lung cancer, is a major contributor to worldwide cancer deaths. Although the slit guidance ligand (SLIT) protein family is implicated in both normal biological processes and disease states, the specific role of SLIT2 in LUAD development remains unclear.

pmc-12682536.title: Delayed non ischemic cerebral enhancing lesions after endovascular stent assisted coiling of an unruptured intracranial aneurysm, a case description followed by a literature analysis on the probable causes, differential diagnosis and treatment
pmc-12682536.creator: Chris Noel Leung Chung Tseung, Jiaqi Dai, Min Wang, Tianwen Gao, Hua Lu, Zhaolu Wang
pmc-12682536.description: Trial (ISAT trial) (1) showed that endovascular coiling was more likely to result in independent survival at 1 year post procedure compared to neurosurgical clipping for ruptured intracranial aneurysm patients. Intravascular aneurysm coiling also result in a generally shorter length of hospital stay and lower overall treatment cost than surgical clipping (2).

pmc-12699271.title: Insights into the microbiome of mine drainage from the Mária mine in Rožňava, Slovakia: a metagenomic approach
pmc-12699271.creator: Lenka Hagarová, Daniel Kupka
pmc-12699271.description: The Mária mine, particularly the Strieborná vein, in Rožňava, is one of the most important mines in Slovakia, containing Ag-bearing tetrahedrite (40–46 wt% Cu, 26 wt% Sb, ~1 wt% Ag), making it an important source of strategic and critical raw materials. This mine discharges a unique neutral-pH (6.9), metal-rich mine water drainage (402 mg L−1 SO42−, 4.

pmc-13239841.title: Treatment Outcomes of Presacral Pilonidal Sinus Disease Using Crystallised Phenol: A Single‐Centre Clinical Series
pmc-13239841.creator: Berkan Acar, Ali Muhtaroğlu, Murat Akalin, Elif Yilmaz, Mehmet Yildiz
pmc-13239841.description: Objective: To evaluate short‐term treatment outcomes and treatment burden in patients with presacral pilonidal sinus disease managed with crystallised phenol in a single‐centre clinical series, with particular emphasis on the relationship between pit burden and session requirement. Methods: Consecutive patients treated with crystallised phenol were analysed (n = 40).

pmc-13240966.title: Parental motivations, facilitators, and barriers to participating in a pediatric vaccine trial in Kathmandu, Nepal: A qualitative study
pmc-13240966.creator: Charlie Firth, Neha Kumari Das, Erina Khatri, Sanjeev Bijukchhe, Sachi Chuke, Benjamin Curtis, Meeru Gurung, Sarah Kelly, Elizabeth O’Mahony, Andrew J Pollard, Arun Kumar Sharma, Shrijana Shrestha, Samantha Vanderslott, Bipin Adhikari
pmc-13240966.description: Pediatric vaccine trials are essential for generating evidence to inform immunization policy, yet their success depends on effective recruitment and sustained participation of children and their caregivers. Understanding parental decision-making is particularly important in low- and middle-income countries, where sociocultural dynamics, trust, and access to healthcare may shape willingness to participate in research.

pmc-13290941.title: Efficacy of hydrocolloid dressing for hand-foot skin reaction: J-SUPPORT 1701 APRON trial
pmc-13290941.creator: Asako Ryu, Sadamoto Zenda, Yoichi Shimizu, Atsuo Takashima, Arata Tsutsumida, Akira Takahashi, Michiko Arai, Chigusa Morizane, Takuhiro Yamaguchi, Yusuke Takagi, Tomoe Mashiko, Tempei Miyaji, Takashi Kawaguchi, Naoya Yamazaki

pmc-13319787.title: Association between serum uric acid level and cataract Arisk: A cross-sectional study based on two databases (CHARLS and NHANES)
pmc-13319787.creator: Hu Lumei, Wang Guoqing, Yi Xianglong
pmc-13319787.description: ObjectiveCataracts represent the predominant cause of global blindness. Although previous research has implicated aqueous humor uric acid in cataract pathogenesis, its invasive measurement method limits clinical utility. Consequently, the association between readily accessible serum uric acid levels and cataract risk remains poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate this relationship in two large, independent populations.
